redesign.idea: Morphing conformal diagram driven by a/m.
redesign.interaction: Slide a/m toward 1 and watch region II diamonds shrink to zero width and the diagram collapse into the zigzag column.

figures.label: Fig. 20.8
figures.caption_paraphrase: Two-sheeted maximal extension of super-extremal Kerr.
figures.visual_description: Two copies of a meridional plane side by side, labelled (x, z)-plane and (x', z')-plane. Each has a vertical symmetry axis theta = 0 with a rotation arrow phi, solid hyperbola-like curves labelled theta = constant, dashed confocal ellipses labelled r = constant, and a thick horizontal segment along the equator theta = pi/2 (the disc seen edge-on) whose endpoints are marked as the singularity. Curved lines labelled 'Identify' join the top face of the left disc to the bottom face of the right disc and vice versa.
figures.what_it_teaches: How to continue r through the disc bounded by the ring into a second, negative-r copy of space.

redesign.idea: 3D wormhole-through-a-disc explorer: two stacked copies of space with confocal spheroids, where a probe passing through the disc emerges in the other sheet.
redesign.interaction: Fly a probe along any path; its colour indicates the sign of r; passing through the disc once flips sheet, twice returns; readout of the mass seen from far away (positive or negative).

figures.label: Fig. 20.9
figures.caption_paraphrase: Super-extremal Kerr viewed as a naked singularity.
figures.visual_description: Equatorial view: a wavy circle at the centre is the ring singularity, surrounded by a circle labelled stationary limit surface. Large black dots are scattered outside, small cone/triangle symbols lie inside. A light signal starting near the ring spirals outward through several turns with arrowheads, crosses the stationary limit surface, and ends at an eye symbol at top left labelled 'Escaping light signal'.
figures.what_it_teaches: Without horizons, light from the singularity can reach distant observers by spiralling out with the rotation.

redesign.idea: Ray tracer for equatorial null geodesics of Kerr with adjustable spin.
redesign.interaction: Slider a/m crossing 1; emit rays from near r = 0; for a < m every ray is captured behind r_+, for a > m some rays spiral to infinity and are highlighted as reaching the observer.

figures.label: Fig. 20.10
figures.visual_description: A vase of flowers (upper left) and a boxy television set (upper right) each have an arrow pointing down into a large dark stippled disc representing a black hole.
figures.what_it_teaches: Whatever falls in, the final black hole keeps no memory of it apart from mass, spin and charge.

redesign.idea: Drop-anything black hole: learner drags objects with different shapes, spins and charges into a hole whose display lists only m, J, Q.
redesign.interaction: Drag objects in; the three numbers update and the horizon shape (oblateness of the ergosphere) responds; a 'rewind' button plays the white-hole time reverse.

figures.label: Fig. 20.11
figures.caption_paraphrase: Imaginary engineering scheme for extracting energy from a rotating hole.
figures.visual_description: A large circular truss framework surrounds a central black hole; an 'energy extraction unit' sits on the framework at the top. A dashed trajectory of dots labelled 'Matter in' runs down to the centre; a second dashed trajectory of open circles labelled 'Energized matter out' runs back up to the unit. At the centre a hatched disc (outer event horizon) is surrounded by a circle (stationary limit surface), and a 'Particle decay' point with an arrow lies between them in the ergosphere.
figures.what_it_teaches: The Penrose process: split a particle in the ergosphere so that one piece falls in and the other returns with more energy than was sent.

redesign.idea: Penrose process simulator on equatorial Kerr geodesics with conserved Killing energy readouts.
redesign.interaction: Choose spin, entry trajectory and the split point and momentum sharing; see the infalling fragment's Killing energy (negative only inside the ergosphere), the escaping energy gain, and the resulting drop in the hole's J and m; a meter tracks cumulative extraction toward the irreducible-mass limit.

figures.label: Fig. 20.12
figures.caption_paraphrase: A region V on a hypersurface with its boundary U used for the charge integral.
figures.visual_description: A slanted parallelogram representing the spacelike hypersurface, containing an ellipse labelled V with its boundary labelled U = dV.
figures.what_it_teaches: Setting of the divergence theorem: a volume on a slice and its bounding 2-surface.

redesign.idea: Flux-at-infinity demo: a slice with sources inside a draggable, stretchable 2-surface; the flux readout stays constant while the surface encloses the same sources, for both electric flux and Komar mass.
redesign.interaction: Drag and resize the surface; move sources in or out; toggle between electromagnetism and Schwarzschild Komar integrand.

figures.label: Fig. 20.13
figures.caption_paraphrase: Spacetime cartoon of Hawking pair creation near a horizon.
figures.visual_description: Time arrow t pointing up at left. Two vertical lines represent the event horizon. Lens-shaped closed loops with arrows depict virtual pairs created and annihilated (labelled creation of a particle-antiparticle pair, annihilation of pair, virtual pair), one loop straddling a horizon line. V-shaped paths show an antiparticle falling into the hole while a particle escapes to infinity, and an upper V shows the same event reinterpreted as a particle escaping backwards in time and then scattered by the gravitational field forwards in time.
figures.what_it_teaches: A heuristic picture of Hawking radiation as pair separation at the horizon, with the Feynman-Stueckelberg backward-in-time reading as quantum tunnelling.

redesign.idea: Pair-creation animation on an Eddington-Finkelstein diagram with a mass slider driving the Hawking temperature and lifetime.
redesign.interaction: Slider M from asteroid to solar mass; animate pair creation near r = 2M; readouts for T (showing it rises as M falls), peak wavelength and evaporation time; a toggle reinterprets the infalling antiparticle as a backward-moving particle.

worked_examples.problem: Produce the Kerr metric from Schwarzschild without solving the field equations.
worked_examples.method: Write Schwarzschild's inverse metric in advanced EF coordinates, factor it as a null tetrad, complexify r in a prescribed way, apply the complex shift in v and r by i a cos(theta), demand real v' and r', and rebuild g^ab from the new tetrad.
worked_examples.key_insight: Rotation enters through an imaginary displacement of the radial and null coordinates along the axis; the null tetrad is the natural object on which to perform it.
worked_examples.result: Kerr tetrad (20.21) and advanced EF line element (20.22)

worked_examples.problem: Convert the Kerr metric from advanced EF to Boyer-Lindquist form.
worked_examples.method: Use the differential transformation dv = dt + (r^2 + a^2)/Delta dr, dphi-bar = dphi + a/Delta dr and simplify, noticing that the line element can be grouped into two squares.
worked_examples.key_insight: Removing all dr cross terms isolates a single dt dphi term and makes t- and phi-independence obvious.

worked_examples.problem: Show that writing flat space in a rotating frame generates a time-azimuth cross term like Kerr's.
worked_examples.method: Substitute phi = phi' + at into the cylindrical Minkowski metric and expand r^2 dphi^2.
worked_examples.key_insight: A dt dphi term is the metric fingerprint of rotation, though flat-space rigid rotation is only suggestive.
worked_examples.result: ds^2 = (1 - a^2 r^2) dt^2 - 2 a r^2 dphi' dt - (dr^2 + r^2 dphi'^2 + dz^2)

worked_examples.problem: Relate the Boyer-Lindquist r to the Euclidean radius and check asymptotic flatness.
worked_examples.method: Square and add the Kerr-form Cartesian coordinates (20.29) to get R^2, then expand for r >> a; let R -> infinity in (20.28).
worked_examples.key_insight: r labels oblate spheroids; the difference from R dies off as a^2/r.
worked_examples.result: R^2 = r^2 + a^2 sin^2 theta; R = r + a^2 sin^2 theta/(2r) + ...

worked_examples.problem: Locate the singularity, infinite-redshift surfaces and horizons of Kerr.
worked_examples.method: Set rho^2 = 0 and map to Cartesian coordinates; set g_00 = 0 and solve the quadratic in r; compute g^11 and set Delta = 0.
worked_examples.key_insight: Two different conditions (g_00 = 0 and g^11 = 0) that coincide in Schwarzschild separate in Kerr, opening the ergosphere.

worked_examples.problem: Find the Kerr analogues of radial null geodesics.
worked_examples.method: At fixed theta, write first integrals L, N from t and phi, the null condition, and the theta equation; eliminate to find the constraint (N + aL sin^2 theta)(N - aL sin^2 theta) = 0; solve on one branch and integrate dt/dr and dphi/dr by partial fractions.
worked_examples.key_insight: An overdetermined system (four equations, three velocities) is what picks out the special congruences; r is automatically affine.

worked_examples.problem: Build coordinates regular across r_+ from the ingoing principal congruence.
worked_examples.method: Require dt-bar = -dr and dphi-bar = 0 along (20.62)-(20.63), which fixes dt-bar = dt + 2mr/Delta dr and dphi-bar = dphi + a/Delta dr; define v = t-bar + r.
worked_examples.key_insight: Adapting coordinates to infalling light removes the horizon's coordinate singularity, closing the loop with the Newman-Janis form.

worked_examples.problem: Decide where an observer (or photon) can avoid rotating relative to infinity.
worked_examples.method: Constrain a null curve to dr = dtheta = 0, solve the quadratic Boyer-Lindquist null condition for dphi/dt, show the minus-branch denominator is positive for r > r_+, and find when the numerator a sin theta - Delta^{1/2} is non-positive.
worked_examples.key_insight: The best a counter-rotating light ray can do reaches zero angular velocity exactly at S_+; massive observers do worse.

worked_examples.problem: Obtain the Kerr-Newman metric and its horizon and stationary limit (set as an exercise, results quoted).
worked_examples.method: Apply the same complex shift to the Reissner-Nordstrom seed in advanced EF coordinates (the text leaves this as Exercise 20.16); the usual choice, not spelled out in the book, is to complexify the charge term epsilon^2/r^2 as epsilon^2/(r r-bar), which becomes epsilon^2/rho^2.
worked_examples.key_insight: Charge and spin enter additively in the horizon condition: a^2 + epsilon^2 <= m^2.

worked_examples.problem: Check that the flux integral at infinity returns the charge of a point charge.
worked_examples.method: Use Minkowski normals at large r to reduce the integrand to F^tr r^2 sin theta, insert F^tr = q/(4 pi r^2) and integrate over the sphere.
worked_examples.key_insight: Total charge is encoded entirely in the 1/r^2 tail of the field.

worked_examples.problem: Evaluate the Komar integral for Schwarzschild and fix its normalization.
worked_examples.method: Take K = d/dt; normalize n^a and m^a with g_00 and g_11; the product of normalization factors cancels so the integrand is nabla_0 K_1; reduce to g_00 Gamma^0_01 (magnitude m/r^2) and integrate over the sphere.
worked_examples.key_insight: The r^2 from the area cancels the 1/r^2 of the field at every radius, so the answer is independent of where the sphere is placed in vacuum.
worked_examples.result: E_total = m (up to a sign fixed by orientation)

worked_examples.problem: Estimate the Hawking temperature and evaporation time scale.
worked_examples.method: Insert constants into T = hbar c^3/(8 pi G k_B M) for M = M_sun; quote the lifetime scale.
worked_examples.key_insight: Temperature falls as mass rises, so stellar holes are far colder than the cosmic microwave background and evaporation is runaway only at small mass.
worked_examples.result: About 6x10^-8 K for a solar mass; about 10^67 years to evaporate

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: A flat spacetime written in rotating coordinates
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: The dt dphi' cross term that appears when Minkowski space is expressed in a turning frame is offered as the reason to read Kerr's dt dphi term as rotation.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: In flat space the cross term is removable by undoing the rotation; in Kerr it is not, and the authors admit rigid rotation in relativity is not treated.
analogies_and_intuitions.app_idea: Side-by-side metric panels: flat rotating coordinates versus Kerr, with a button that 'unrotates' flat space but fails for Kerr.

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: A film of a spinning top run backwards
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: Reversing time for a spinning source looks like the same source spinning the opposite way, matching Kerr's invariance under t -> -t with phi -> -phi.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: Symmetry is only suggestive; many non-rotating metrics with other cross terms could share it.
analogies_and_intuitions.app_idea: Play a rotating-disc video forward and backward next to a flipped mirror; the metric panel shows invariance only for the combined flip.

analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: Horizons, three regions, Penrose diagram and extreme case of Kerr are all described 'as for RN'.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: Kerr is not spherically symmetric; the diagrams are only valid along the axis, and the ring allows passage to negative r which RN lacks.

analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: Charge from a flux of F^ab at infinity is the model for mass from a flux of the Killing-vector derivative, with the constant chosen to give Schwarzschild m.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: Gravity has no local energy density and needs a symmetry (Killing vector) to make the construction work; different constructions (Komar, ADM) can differ outside stationarity.
analogies_and_intuitions.app_idea: Toggle the same draggable Gaussian surface between an electric charge and a Schwarzschild mass.

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: Horizon area as entropy, surface gravity as temperature
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: Area never decreasing parallels the second law; uniform surface gravity parallels uniform equilibrium temperature; the first law links mass change to area change.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: Classical area increase fails once Hawking radiation is included; the correspondence becomes exact only with quantum field theory.

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: Superradiance from a spinning metal sphere
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: The wave amplification off rotating conductors is cited as the analogue of extracting rotational energy from a Kerr hole, via Zel'dovich.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: Superradiance is a wave phenomenon; the Penrose process is particle kinematics; Hawking radiation does not need rotation at all.

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: Virtual pairs split by a horizon; an antiparticle as a particle running backwards in time
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: One member of a vacuum pair falls in while the other escapes; reinterpreted, a particle tunnels out of the hole backwards in time and is scattered forward.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: A heuristic cartoon, not a derivation; it does not explain the thermal spectrum or why T scales as 1/M.

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: Vase of flowers and a television set disappearing into a black hole
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: Wheeler's cartoon makes vivid that no details of the swallowed objects survive except m, a and charge; time-reversed, objects popping out would betray a white hole.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: Hides the dynamical settling process and the conditions of the uniqueness theorems.

analogies_and_intuitions.analogy: A civilization living off a black hole
analogies_and_intuitions.how_used: Framework around a rotating hole sends matter into the ergosphere and harvests the returning energized fragments.
analogies_and_intuitions.limits: Engineering fantasy; the maximum extractable energy is limited by the irreducible mass (not stated in the text).

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: A co-rotating coordinate system should turn Kerr into Schwarzschild, just as a rotating Newtonian source can be viewed at rest.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: No coordinate change maps Kerr to Schwarzschild; the rotation is encoded in curvature, and the nonlinear field equations tie the exterior field to the spinning source.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: In Newtonian mechanics rotation is always frame-relative.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: The Boyer-Lindquist r is the ordinary distance from the centre.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: r labels oblate spheroids; the Euclidean radius satisfies R^2 = r^2 + a^2 sin^2 theta, so r = 0 is a disc, not a point.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: It reduces to the Schwarzschild r when a = 0 and has the same name.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: The surface of infinite redshift is always the event horizon.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: In Kerr the stationary limit surface S_+ lies outside r_+ except at the poles; they coincide only in the static limit or on the axis.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: In Schwarzschild both conditions give r = 2m.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: Once inside the stationary limit surface you are trapped.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: S_+ is timelike (except at the poles), so particles cross it in both directions; only r_+ is a one-way surface.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Infinite redshift and horizon were the same thing before.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: The Kerr singularity is a point at the centre.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: It is a ring of radius a in the equatorial plane, timelike and avoidable, bounding a disc through which one can pass to negative r.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Schwarzschild's r = 0 and Newtonian point masses.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: Nothing, not even energy, can ever be extracted from a black hole classically.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: In the Penrose process energy is extracted from a rotating hole at the expense of its angular momentum, using the ergosphere, which lies outside the horizon.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: The popular slogan that nothing escapes.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: Singularity theorems prove that curvature becomes infinite.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: They prove causal geodesic incompleteness and inextendibility; infinite curvature is the most plausible but unproved explanation.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: Singularities in exact solutions are artefacts of their symmetry and would vanish in realistic, asymmetric collapse.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: Penrose's 1965 theorem and its successors show that incompleteness persists under generic perturbations given trapped surfaces and energy conditions.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: That was the prevailing view before 1965.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: Only rotating black holes can radiate.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: Hawking showed all black holes emit thermal radiation when quantum effects are included; rotation is not needed.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Energy extraction and superradiance were first discussed for rotating holes.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: The Kerr parameter a is an angular velocity.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: a = J/m is angular momentum per unit mass (a length in geometrized units); the horizon's angular velocity is a different quantity, a/(r_+^2 + a^2).
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: The text itself says a is related to angular velocity, and the same letter is used for the angular velocity of the rotating frame in (20.37).

misconceptions_addressed.correction: Hawking temperature is inversely proportional to mass; a solar-mass hole is at about 6x10^-8 K and more massive ones are colder.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: Intuition from stars, and the printed scaling (M/M_sun) x 6x10^-8 K in the text.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: The Newman-Janis trick is a derivation that always produces valid rotating solutions.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: It is a heuristic that happens to work for Schwarzschild and RN seeds; it is not justified by the field equations, and the result must be checked.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: It is presented as a clean procedure that gives the right answer.

misconceptions_addressed.misconception: Horizon area can never decrease under any circumstances.
misconceptions_addressed.correction: The area theorem assumes a classical energy condition; Hawking evaporation violates it, and the area shrinks as the hole loses mass, while total generalized entropy still increases.
misconceptions_addressed.why_tempting: The chapter states area increase as a law and later describes evaporation without reconciling them.

thought_experiments.name: Photon trying to hover against the spin
thought_experiments.setup: Light is guided to move at fixed r and theta around a Kerr hole, aimed opposite to the rotation, and we ask its angular velocity seen from infinity.
thought_experiments.lesson: At S_+ even light cannot make headway against the rotation, so no massive observer can be at rest there or inside.
thought_experiments.app_idea: Race a counter-rotating photon and rocket at chosen r; plot dphi/dt against r with the zero crossing at S_+.

thought_experiments.name: Collapse of a rotating star through both horizons
thought_experiments.setup: A spinning star with Kerr exterior collapses; follow an observer riding its surface through r_+, then r_-.
thought_experiments.lesson: Crossing r_+ is irreversible and crossing r_- is forced, but unlike Schwarzschild the collapse can halt in region III and the extension suggests emergence into a new universe.
concepts: gravitational collapse to a rotating black hole

thought_experiments.name: Travelling through the ring
thought_experiments.setup: An observer in the extended Kerr spacetime passes through the disc bounded by the ring singularity.
thought_experiments.lesson: They emerge where r < 0, in an asymptotically flat region whose mass looks negative, and near the ring can find closed timelike curves.

thought_experiments.name: Meeting yourself in the past
thought_experiments.setup: An observer follows one of the closed timelike curves in region III.
thought_experiments.lesson: Causality is violated: such an observer returns to their own earlier events, suggesting the inner Kerr regions are unphysical.

thought_experiments.name: Penrose process
thought_experiments.setup: A particle is fired into the ergosphere where it splits; one fragment falls inward, the other flies out.
thought_experiments.lesson: The escaping fragment can carry away more mass-energy than came in, drawn from the hole's rotational energy.

thought_experiments.name: Objects popping out of nowhere
thought_experiments.setup: A space traveller sees a vase of flowers and a television set suddenly appear.
thought_experiments.lesson: Time-reversing the no-hair collapse describes a white hole, which would emit rather than absorb.

thought_experiments.name: Black hole in a thermal bath
thought_experiments.setup: Place a black hole with finite entropy (hence finite temperature) inside radiation at the same temperature.
thought_experiments.lesson: Classically it could only absorb, so no equilibrium is possible; the paradox is resolved only if the hole emits, which Hawking showed it does.

historical_notes.event: Kerr discovered the rotating vacuum solution by searching among metrics of the flat-plus-null-square type and wrote it in Cartesian-type coordinates.
historical_notes.significance: First exact rotating black-hole solution; the year is general knowledge, not given in the text.

historical_notes.event: Complex-transformation trick relating Schwarzschild to Kerr (and RN to Kerr-Newman) on a null tetrad.
historical_notes.significance: Provides a short route to Kerr that this chapter adopts; year from general knowledge.

historical_notes.event: Coordinates generalizing Schwarzschild coordinates to Kerr.
historical_notes.significance: Standard coordinates for Kerr's properties; year from general knowledge.

historical_notes.event: Weak-field exterior field of a rotating sphere.
historical_notes.significance: Used as supporting evidence that ma is the Kerr angular momentum; year from general knowledge.

historical_notes.event: Reinterpretation of Schwarzschild as a black hole with a curvature singularity at r = 0.
historical_notes.significance: Marked the modern acceptance of black holes after four decades of dismissing the Schwarzschild singularities.

historical_notes.event: First singularity theorem, introducing trapped surfaces and geodesic incompleteness.
historical_notes.significance: Showed that departures from spherical symmetry do not avert collapse to a singularity.

historical_notes.event: Hawking's cosmological singularity result using a past trapped surface, followed by a series of papers culminating in the Hawking-Penrose theorem of 1970.
historical_notes.significance: Established singularity theorems as a central achievement of modern GR.

historical_notes.event: Proposal of energy extraction from the ergosphere of a rotating black hole and of the cosmic censorship hypothesis.
historical_notes.significance: Showed black holes can be energy sources and framed the naked-singularity problem.

historical_notes.event: Suggested that rotating black holes, like spinning metal spheres, should amplify and emit radiation (superradiance).
historical_notes.significance: A precursor of the discovery of Hawking radiation.

historical_notes.event: Coined the 'no hair' description with the cartoon of objects falling into a hole.
Killing-vector surface integral for mass (year from general knowledge).
historical_notes.significance: Standard definition of mass for stationary spacetimes.

historical_notes.event: ADM Hamiltonian formulation giving a boundary-integral mass.
historical_notes.significance: Mass for general asymptotically flat spacetimes.

historical_notes.event: Proof of the positive energy theorem (year from general knowledge).
historical_notes.significance: Guarantees stability-like positivity of total mass under the dominant energy condition.

historical_notes.event: Discovery that black holes emit thermal radiation (year from general knowledge).
historical_notes.significance: Turned black-hole thermodynamics from analogy into physics and implied evaporation.

applications_and_observations.details: Collapse radiates away asymmetries once a horizon forms, leaving a stationary Kerr-Newman hole described by mass, spin and charge; realistic astrophysical holes are expected to be essentially uncharged Kerr.
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: Horizon exists if a^2 + epsilon^2 <= m^2; for Kerr, r_+ ranges from 2m (a = 0) to m (a = m).

applications_and_observations.details: S_+ reaches 2m at the equator for any spin and meets the horizon at the poles; the ergosphere is thickest for maximal spin (own reading of (20.46)-(20.47)).
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: Extremal Kerr: equatorial ergosphere from r = m to r = 2m (Boyer-Lindquist).

applications_and_observations.details: The text gives no numbers. Own addition: the rotational energy that can in principle be extracted is the difference between m and the irreducible mass, at most about 29% of the mass for an extremal hole.
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: M_irr = sqrt(r_+^2 + a^2)/2; extremal: 1 - 1/sqrt2 ~ 0.29 (own estimate, not in text).

applications_and_observations.topic: Hawking temperature of stellar black holes
applications_and_observations.details: Evaluates T = hbar c^3/(8 pi G k_B M); stellar holes are far colder than the 2.7 K microwave background, so they currently absorb more than they emit (comparison is own).
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: About 6x10^-8 K x (M_sun/M) (text prints the ratio inverted).

applications_and_observations.details: Evaporation accelerates as mass decreases; a solar-mass hole would take about 10^67 years.
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: ~10^67 yr for M_sun; lifetime scales as M^3 (scaling is own addition).

applications_and_observations.topic: Primordial black holes as gamma-ray sources
applications_and_observations.details: Mini holes from the early universe could be finishing evaporation now and producing high-energy gamma bursts; comparisons with gamma-ray observations had been inconclusive.
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: Text uses about 10 billion years since the big bang (current value 13.8 Gyr); holes near 5x10^11 kg would be ending now (own estimate).

applications_and_observations.details: No physically realistic matter source is known that matches onto the Kerr exterior; a toroidal source is speculated because of the ring singularity.

notation_and_conventions.convention: Signature (+, -, -, -); geometrized units G = c = 1 throughout, except SI units in the Hawking temperature (20.98).
Latin i, j label tetrad legs and are moved with the frame metric g_ij; Latin a, b are tensor indices moved with g_ab.
notation_and_conventions.notes: Later in §20.12, i, j = 1, 2, 3 denote spatial coordinate indices in the ADM integral.

notation_and_conventions.convention: l.n = +1 and m.m-bar = -1, suited to signature (+---).
notation_and_conventions.notes: Books using (-+++) take l.n = -1 and m.m-bar = +1.

notation_and_conventions.convention: rho^2 = r^2 + a^2 cos^2 theta; Delta = r^2 - 2mr + a^2.
notation_and_conventions.notes: In ch19 Delta denoted the constant m^2 - epsilon^2; here it is the r-dependent horizon function.

notation_and_conventions.convention: (x^0, x^1, x^2, x^3) = (v, r, theta, phi) in the tetrad construction and (t, r, theta, phi) in Boyer-Lindquist; bars mark advanced-type coordinates (t-bar, phi-bar) with v = t-bar + r.
r_{S+/-} for infinite-redshift surfaces S_+/-; r_+/- for horizons (figures use superscripts r^+, r^-, S^+).
Black-hole charge is epsilon (geometrized Gaussian), not Q; Q denotes total electric charge only in §20.12.
n^a and m^a are null tetrad legs in §20.1-20.2 but unit timelike normal to Sigma and unit spacelike normal to the 2-surface in §20.12; m also denotes the mass.
notation_and_conventions.notes: Easy source of confusion when reading (20.86)-(20.88).

notation_and_conventions.convention: Derivative with respect to an affine parameter along a geodesic.
Lorentz-Heaviside units in the point-charge check, so F^tr = q/(4 pi r^2).
gamma is the determinant of the induced positive-definite 3-metric on Sigma; sigma that of the induced 2-metric on the boundary surface.
mu energy density; p_alpha (alpha = 1, 2, 3) principal stresses of T_ab.

difficulty.notes: The first half is heavy index and algebra work (complex tetrads, long line elements, geodesic eliminations) with most verification left to exercises; the Newman-Janis step is unmotivated magic for newcomers. Conceptually the chapter is dense with genuinely strange ideas - ring singularity, negative-r universes, closed timelike curves, naked singularities, ergosphere - presented mainly by analogy with RN and with only axis Penrose diagrams. The final three sections are descriptive surveys, easier to read but offering little derivation for the Komar/ADM, singularity-theorem and Hawking material.

teaching_gems.gem: Get a rotating solution by complex-shifting a static one on a null tetrad, then immediately sanity-check the a -> 0 limit.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Replaces a notoriously long integration with a few steps and shows why null tetrads are worth learning; the limit check anchors trust.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Step-through animation: a symbolic panel shows the tetrad at each stage while a 3D view of r = const surfaces morphs from spheres to oblate spheroids as a is dialled up.

teaching_gems.gem: Read spin off the metric without dynamics: invariance only under joint reversal of t and phi, plus a dt dphi term like a rotating frame.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Uses symmetry reasoning learners already trust and a flat-space calculation they can do in two lines.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Symmetry toggles (t -> -t, phi -> -phi, a -> -a) applied to a live metric; the metric highlights which terms change sign, showing only the combined flips leave it unchanged.

teaching_gems.gem: Separate two conditions that coincided for Schwarzschild: g_00 = 0 (infinite redshift) and g^11 = 0 (null r = const). Their gap is the ergosphere.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Turns a new structure into a contrast with something familiar, and explains why the horizon and redshift surface are different notions.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Dual plot of g_00 and g^11 versus r at chosen theta with a spin slider; shaded band where the two differ maps onto the 3D ergosphere.

teaching_gems.gem: Define the stationary limit operationally: force light to circle at fixed r and theta, aim it against the spin, and find where it stalls.
teaching_gems.why_effective: A physical test replaces abstract Killing-vector language; the formula yields a clean inequality.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Plot the two branches of dphi/dt from (20.70) against r; the counter-rotating branch crosses zero at S_+, animated with a pair of photons on a ring.

teaching_gems.gem: Wavefront diagram in the equatorial plane: whether an emitter sits inside its own light front encodes static, forced co-rotation, and forced infall.
teaching_gems.why_effective: A purely spatial picture of light-cone tilting, readable without Penrose diagrams.
teaching_gems.app_idea: See Fig. 20.5 redesign: clickable flash-bulbs with spin slider.

teaching_gems.gem: Picture r through a disc: confocal ellipsoids collapse to a disc at r = 0; glue its faces crosswise to a second copy of space to reach negative r.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Makes an analytic continuation tangible and explains how the ring bounds a passage.
teaching_gems.app_idea: 3D probe fly-through with sheet colouring (Fig. 20.8 redesign).

teaching_gems.gem: Build gravitational mass by copying Gauss's law: current -> Ricci times Killing vector, divergence theorem -> surface flux, normalization fixed by Schwarzschild.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Leverages a mastered electromagnetic idea and shows why a symmetry is needed to define energy in GR.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Draggable Gaussian surface with a toggle between electric flux and Komar integrand; readout constant in vacuum.

teaching_gems.gem: Present all singularity theorems as one template with three slots: boundary/initial condition, energy (curvature) condition, causality condition.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Gives learners a memorable scaffold for a family of technical theorems they will not prove.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Card-slot widget: learner picks a trapped surface or cosmological condition, an energy condition, a causality assumption; the widget names the resulting theorem and lists counterexamples when a slot is removed (e.g. Kerr's CTCs, de Sitter violating the strong condition).

teaching_gems.gem: No-hair told as a cartoon and inverted into a joke about white holes.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Humour fixes a deep uniqueness result in memory and introduces time reversal of black holes.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Drop-anything black hole with rewind button (Fig. 20.10 redesign).

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The Newman-Janis trick is presented without any reason why it works, and the choice of how to complexify r (which r become r-bar) is not justified.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners may think it is a general derivation, or feel the result is conjured.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Say plainly that it is a heuristic verified afterwards by checking the vacuum equations; show that other complexifications fail; mention it does not generate general rotating interior or non-vacuum solutions.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Printed misprints: (20.33) has a^2 + y^2 instead of a^2 + r^2; (20.43) has x dy - y dz instead of x dy - y dx; the RN seed on p.385 has dr^2 instead of dv^2; the normalization before (20.88) has (m^0)^2 instead of (m^1)^2; Exercise 20.2 cites (16.24) instead of (17.24).
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Students checking the algebra will get stuck or distrust correct reasoning.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Show corrected equations in the app and flag them in tutor responses.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The Hawking temperature scale is printed as (M/M_sun) x 6x10^-8 K, i.e. proportional to mass, contradicting (20.98) and the preceding sentence.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Reinforces the misconception that bigger black holes are hotter.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Use T ~ 6x10^-8 K x (M_sun/M) and stress the negative heat capacity.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: In (20.89)-(20.90) the sign of nabla_0 K_1 is dropped: a direct calculation gives -m/r^2, so a positive mass requires choosing the inward-pointing normal or an overall sign in the definition, none of which is discussed.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: A careful student obtains E = -m and cannot find the error.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: State orientation conventions for n^a and m^a explicitly or define the Komar integral with the conventional sign; also note the Komar normalization differs (factor 2) for angular momentum.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Infinite-redshift surfaces are identified with g_00 = 0 by assertion, and horizons with g^11 = 0, without explaining that the horizon generator is the combination d/dt + Omega_H d/dphi or defining surface gravity.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: The thermodynamics section then refers to surface gravity with no formula and no link to Kerr.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Introduce the horizon angular velocity Omega_H = a/(r_+^2 + a^2) and kappa = (r_+ - r_-)/(2(r_+^2 + a^2)); show kappa -> 0 at extremality.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The statement that any spacetime with a forming horizon approaches Kerr-Newman is described as a proved theorem.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Overstates what is rigorously known; the uniqueness theorems concern stationary holes and nonlinear stability of Kerr is only partly proved.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Distinguish stationary uniqueness theorems from the final-state conjecture; mention recent stability results for slowly rotating Kerr.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Area increase is stated as a law and evaporation is described afterwards, but the conflict (evaporation shrinks the horizon) is never addressed, and the entropy formula S = A/4 is omitted.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners are left with two incompatible statements and no quantitative entropy.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Add the generalized second law and S_BH = k_B c^3 A/(4 G hbar).

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The Penrose process is purely verbal: no negative Killing energy, no efficiency, no irreducible mass.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Hard to see why the ergosphere is essential or how much energy is available.

tutor_notes: Open with: 'What would you expect to change about a black hole if the star that formed it was spinning?' Collect guesses (flattening, dragging, stronger or weaker horizon) and return to them after §20.5.

Recommended order: Boyer-Lindquist metric and its a -> 0 limit first, then the three rotation clues, then g_00 = 0 versus Delta = 0 and the ergosphere picture, then principal congruences and EF coordinates, then global structure; treat the Newman-Janis construction as optional enrichment for learners comfortable with tetrads.
Whenever Kerr shows a new feature, ask the learner what the Schwarzschild analogue was; the chapter is built as a replay, so this keeps them oriented.
Check for understanding: 'Can you be inside the ergosphere and still escape? Can you be inside the stationary limit surface and stay at rest?' (yes; no).
Check for understanding: 'Where is the Kerr singularity, and what shape is r = 0?' Expect a ring of radius a and a disc; probe whether they know r is not Euclidean radius.
When learners ask 'what is a?' answer J/M (a length in G = c = 1), give the bound a <= m for a horizon, and warn that the book loosely calls it an angular velocity.

Common question: 'Is the inner region with negative r and time machines real?' Explain that it belongs to the idealized eternal solution; the inner horizon is believed unstable and realistic collapse is not expected to produce it.
Correct the printed Hawking temperature scaling whenever Hawking radiation comes up: T is about 6x10^-8 K times M_sun/M; larger holes are colder.

For §20.12, first redo the electric Gauss-law argument with the learner, then substitute R^ab K_b for j^a; point out the sign/orientation subtlety in the Schwarzschild check rather than letting it derail them.

For singularity theorems, have the learner fill the three slots for Penrose 1965 (trapped surface, null convergence, a causality/global condition) and Hawking-Penrose 1970, then ask which slot Kerr's interior violates (causality: closed timelike curves).

Useful numbers to have ready (own): r_+ = 2m at a = 0 and m at a = m; equatorial S_+ always at 2m; maximum extractable rotational energy about 29% of m; solar-mass Hawking temperature about 6x10^-8 K.

Distinguish what the chapter proves (horizon locations, stationary limit criterion, Komar mass of Schwarzschild) from what it only reports (no-hair, Penrose process efficiencies, positive energy, singularity theorems, Hawking radiation) so learners calibrate their confidence.
